Guidance & outlook: As a result, consolidated adjusted operating EBITDA improved from negative ₹326 crores in Q4 FY26 to negative ₹195 crores in Q1 FY27.
As this base matures, service can increasingly develop into a recurring, high -margin revenue stream, with our roadmap targeting service revenue of approximately ₹400-500 crore by FY 2027-28.
Over the next couple of quarters, we expect opex to come down into the ₹300-325 crore range, which is where our target is.
Growth & demand: Auto revenue grew 72% sequentially to ₹455 crore, with gross profit of ₹139 crore.
The broader electric two-wheeler market grew approximately 17% quarter-on-quarter, while Ola registrations grew 97%, taking our market share from 5.1% to 8.4%.

Ola Electric Mobility Limited August 07, 2026 The balance sheet strengthened during the quarter through the successful completion of a ₹780 crore QIP, giving us greater financial flexibility as we pursue the next phase of our growth.
Margins & costs: Despite a challenging commodity environment, we sustained Auto gross margin at 30.5%, reflecting the underlying strength of our product economics.
Consolidated operating expenses declined 22% quarter-on-quarter to ₹333 crores, and we remain focused on moving towards a steady- state operating cost base.
Margins remained steady and industry-leading at above 30%, despite the commodity upcycle.
Capex & expansion: Continuing with the Cell business, the full 6 GWh capacity will be commissioned this quarter.
We do not foresee material capex after that, and the remaining Cell capex is funded through debt; the equity contribution is largely complete.
Rishi, except for the Cell project that is now being completed, capex beyond that will be around ₹30-50 crore.
Balance sheet & cash: Our objective is to grow on this leaner operating base and progressively translate incremental revenue and gross profit into operating leverage, taking us towards break-even and sustainable profitability.

As we look ahead, our priorities are clear: scale volumes on a leaner cost base, drive operating leverage, deepen vertical integration, broaden distribution and lifecycle monetisation, and remain disciplined on capital and cash.
Risks & challenges: From some of the challenging quarters in the past, we have now achieved a good balance in the business between growth, gross -margin stability and operating-cost improvement.
Most of the service challenges are now behind us, Akshay.
Whenever parts were required, some were in short supply, particularly a few critical parts where we faced vendor challenges, including issues linked to the macro geopolitical situation.

guidance.t: Our gross -margin target is around 30 -32%, which is where we want it to be, and opex continues to improve structurally.
Rishi, except for the Cell project that is now being completed, capex beyond that will be around ₹30-50 crore.

Guidance & outlook: Consolidated OpEx, including lease expenses, have meaningfully reduced from 844 crores in Q4 FY2024-25, which is last year, to 428 crores during this Q4 FY2025 -26.
In FY25, we had a 500 plus crore of warranty costs, in FY26, it's only 60 crores, 59 crores to be accurate.

Deepak Rastogi - Chief Financial Officer, Ola Electric Mobility Limited: − Looking ahead to Q1 FY27, we expect 40,000 to 45,000 orders and consolidated revenue of 500 to 550 crores, nearly double of the Q4 level.
Growth & demand: So the company is highly focused on ramping up the supply chain quickly enough so that we can, we can fulfill these orders, the backlog also, and I actually expect as we improve our delivery timelines, volumes will go up another 10 -20% in the near term.
Bikes are also there and our market share in bikes is 50% plus.
Ola now has 50% market share in electric motorcycles, and bikes contributed 15% of April gross orders.
Margins & costs: We exited the year with industry-leading gross margins at 38.5%, a much lower cost base, sharply improved execution metrics, better product quality, our first operating cash flow positive quarter, and a Gigafactory which is now entering a scale-up. − This progress comes at an important moment for India.
So for FY26, consolidated revenue stood at 2,253 crores with 173,794 deliveries and consolidated gross margin improved to 30.6%.

Together, the asset base can support approximately 15,000 to 20,000 crores of annual revenue scale across Auto and Cell without needing meaningful incremental CapEx. − With the reset OpEx base and current gross margin structure, adjusted operating EBITDA breakeven is ach ievable at around 20,000 to 25,000 units per month, subject to pricing mix and commodity…
Capex & expansion: And while other competitors will need to do more CapEx as well as new product rollouts, we have our capacity on both automotive and Gigafactory covered because all the CapEx is now behind us.
Like we see that you already have 1 million capac ity in vehicle and, I guess, you will be having just couple of quarters remaining for the CapEx in battery plant. - Mr.
Vipul, in Auto, on an annual basis you should expect very incremental CapEx, maybe ₹50-odd crores that's about it.
Balance sheet & cash: Consolidated CFO was 91 crores, supported by strong gross margins, PLI inflows, lower OpEx and tighter working capital discipline.
The Auto business delivered 213 crores of CFO and 173 crores of free cash flow in Q4.
I think through this year, we'll have about ₹400 plus crores of debt repayments and we might also choose to accelerate some because right now our cost of debt is slightly higher. - Mr.
Risks & challenges: Obviously, in the short term, there will be commodity pressures, as well as some of this gross margin in the last month or two we've invested into aggressive growth.

And because of our unique B2C business model, these three metrics also we will publish for future clarity. − Another point I want to add here is on page 8, you see how while this period had service challenges and we were focused on solving them, brand has actually held well.
April registrations were up 20% month-on- month, while the broader E two-wheeler industry declined by more than 22%. − Mr.
